hypothesis: On a domain wide enough to hold the prior's tail every family, Student-t_5 included, reaches the constant (1/6)||kappa_4||^2 of Theorem 3; E01's Student-t departure near t = 3 on the (801, 8) grid is truncation of the prior in the reference. In expectation a regularly varying tail of index nu adds an e^{-nu t} term carried by events of probability ~ alpha^nu, visible in an untruncated scalar quadrature and invisible in any finite sample.
design: Part chain: rho = 0.85, L = 32, 256 chains x 2 reps (rng tag 'e18-chain'), levels 1.0-5.0, grids (801,8), (1601,16), (3201,32), families laplace, bimodal, uniform, student(5), student(7), student(9); squared gap per chain, local slopes, ratio to the predicted constant. Part scalar: untruncated quadrature for unit-variance t_5, t_7, t_9, t_12 and Laplace on a in [-250,250] (125001 points), x in [-40,40].
predeclared_analysis: Ratio to the constant at t = 3, 4, 5 per family and grid; the local slope; for the scalar computation the slope's limit against -min(nu, 8).
